title: finding(plugin-view): `ObjectView`'s new objectui#9462 comment says the hook decides modifier clicks when no host handler is present — `handleClick` returns EARLY on the handler `ObjectView` always passes, so Cmd/Ctrl-click there still degrades to ordinary navigation
body:
Found by the **at-tier clause-② contract review** of PR objectui#9797 (card objectui#9462), and flagged there as ⛔ **not a re-spin cause** — the PR landed on its own merits. Re-verified line by line on merged `main` by the reviewing seat before filing.

## What

`packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`'s `handleRowClick` carries a comment, added by PR objectui#9797, whose closing sentence is false on the path it describes:

> The branches below deliberately do NOT read it: what Cmd/Ctrl/middle-click should do when no host handler is present **is the hook's own decision, taken before this callback runs.**

The hook never gets to make that decision here. `packages/react/src/hooks/useNavigationOverlay.ts` — `handleClick` — **returns early** when an external `onRowClick` is present, and does so **before** its modifier branch:

```
if (onRowClick) {
  onRowClick(record, event);
  return;
}

// Modifier / middle-click → always open in a new browser tab as a full page.
const isModifierClick = !!(
  event && (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey || event.button === 1)
);
```

And `ObjectView` hands `handleRowClick` down **unconditionally** — `:2226` `onRowClick: handleRowClick,` and `:2264` `onRowClick={handleRowClick}`. There is no arm in which the hook's modifier branch runs for this component.

⇒ `handleRowClick`'s own branches read no `event`, so **in a `plugin-view` `ObjectView` with no host `onRowClick`, a Cmd / Ctrl / middle-click still degrades to an ordinary navigation** — the behaviour objectui#9360 and objectui#9462 exist to make reachable.

## Why it is a card rather than a re-spin of the PR that wrote the comment

⛔ Stated by the reviewer and agreed by the accepting seat:

- It is **outside objectui#9462's subject**, which is hosts that DO supply a handler — and for those hosts the payload now arrives correctly.
- It **misleads no published declaration**: the sentence is a function-body `//`, ⛔ not shipped JSDoc, so nothing in any `.d.ts` says it.
- It changes nothing in the review's ① or ②, and the PR's verdict was PASS on its own contents.

⭐ The instructive part is how it was found: the comment is **new**, written by the very PR that repaired the forwarding, and it is wrong about a file the PR did not change. A repair that explains itself by describing a neighbour's behaviour inherits the risk of being wrong about the neighbour.

## Shape of the remedy — ⛔ not decided here

The reviewer's reading, recorded rather than adopted: *"the fix would be a branch in `handleRowClick`, not a declaration change."* ⚠️ That is a **behaviour** change on a published component — a modifier click that today navigates in place would start opening a new tab — so it owes its own grading, and possibly its own ruling about whether `ObjectView` should mirror the hook's convention at all.

⛔ **And the comment is wrong either way.** Whichever way the behaviour question is ruled, the sentence quoted above does not describe this code and should not survive unamended. Those are two separable deliverables and a taker may do only the second.

## Not measured

⛔ Whether any other consumer of `useNavigationOverlay` passes an unconditional `onRowClick` and therefore has the same dead modifier branch — only `ObjectView` was read. ⛔ Whether the `ObjectGrid` / `ListView` / gallery paths differ here; the reviewer's finding is scoped to `plugin-view`'s `ObjectView`. ⛔ Not driven in a browser: this is a code reading of an early return plus an unconditional hand-down, ⛔ not an observed click.

Refs: objectui#9462 / PR objectui#9797 (the repair, and the comment) · the contract-review record, comment `5725942570` on that PR, where the flag was raised · objectui#9360 (the payload the hook forwards) · objectui#9357 (the channel).
